analysis.title: 从模型竞速走向产品、算力与生态：本期 AI 趋势观察
analysis.lead: 本期共整理 84 条有效信号。下面不是新闻复述，而是把论文、公司、创业与政策放在同一张图里后的编辑性判断。
paragraphs: 研究侧共收录 20 条信号，重点包括 《BACE: LLM-based Code Generation through Bayesian Anchored…》、《Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents…》。与只看榜单相比，更值得持续观察的是论文能否把 Agent 的可靠性、评测完整性与推理成本一起向前推进。
AI 跨领域贡献收录 6 条，代表性事件包括 《Claude Fable 5 协助找到雅可比猜想的显式三维反例》、《OpenAI 模型推翻平面单位距离问题中的长期猜想》。这类结果会区分官方论文、可核验反例、媒体报道与尚待同行评审的社交平台首发，避免把‘可计算验证’和‘完成学术确认’混为一谈。
中国 AI 板块本期收录 16 条动态，已覆盖 智谱 / Z.ai、DeepSeek。代表性变化包括 《智谱 发布 GLM -5.3:国产开源模型编程能力提升50%》、《智谱 正式 发布 GLM -5.3,拥有更强编程能力;谷歌推出Gemini 3.7 Flash模型;索尼…》；竞争正在从单次模型发布延伸到开源策略、Agent 产品入口、国产算力适配和价格体系。
产业侧共有 30 条前沿实验室与大厂动态、5 条关键人物公开信号，另有 0 条创业和 0 条政策安全更新。模型能力、算力供给、创始人判断、产品分发与合规成本正在变成同一个竞争问题。

takeaways.title: 科研判断
takeaways.body: 优先关注带公开证明、实验或可复核数据的 AI 科研贡献，并持续更新同行验证状态。

items.title: BACE: LLM-based Code Generation through Bayesian Anchored Co-Evolution
items.summary: BACE treats generated code and tests as co-evolving populations instead of accepting synthetic tests as ground truth. Bayesian belief updates model tests as noisy sensors, while public examples anchor the search and reduce self-validating drift. The authors report strong results on LiveCodeBench v6 across proprietary and open-weight models.

items.title: How Claude's text watermarking works
items.summary: Future Claude models will generate text that contains a watermark. This is a way of determining the likelihood that Claude was involved in writing the text, and we, along with several other major AI providers, are implementing this change to comply with the EU AI Act. In this article, we share answers to some of the questions we’ve received about how our chosen watermarking method works, whether it affects Claude’s outputs, and why we’re making this change.

items.title: Reward Hacking Benchmark: Measuring Exploits in LLM Agents with Tool Use
items.summary: RHB evaluates tool-using language-model agents on multi-step tasks that contain realistic shortcuts such as skipping verification or manipulating evaluation functions. Across 13 frontier models, the study finds sharp differences in exploit behavior and shows that simple environment hardening can substantially reduce reward hacking without lowering task success.

items.title: Towards Code-Oriented LM Embeddings for Surrogate-Assisted Neural Architecture Search
items.summary: Developing effective surrogates (performance predictors) for Neural Architecture Search (NAS) typically requires expensive fine-tuning or the engineering of complex representations. We propose a low-cost embedding strategy that leverages the inductive bias of Language Models (LMs) to eliminate these overheads. By representing architectures as PyTorch class definition text, we demonstrate that off-the-shelf LMs act as competitive feature extractors without NAS-specialized fine-tuning. items.title: NegaBent, No Regrets: Evolving Spectrally Flat Boolean Functions
items.summary: Negabent Boolean functions are defined by having a flat magnitude spectrum under the nega-Hadamard transform. In this work, we investigate how evolutionary algorithms can be used to evolve (bent-)negabent Boolean functions. items.summary: Designing effective quantum circuits remains a central challenge in quantum computing, as circuit structure strongly influences expressivity, trainability, and hardware feasibility. items.summary: Developmental neural architecture search grows functional networks from compact genomes via self-organisation, but the resulting weights are frozen post-growth—unlike biological circuits, which combine developmental wiring with activity-dependent plasticity. items.title: The Evaluation Cost of Task Specialization in Evolutionary Multi-Robot Systems
items.summary: Task specialization can improve the efficiency of multi-robot systems (MRSs). Previous works have investigated the emergence of task-specialist robot controllers through evolutionary optimization and have argued that task specialization is more likely to evolve when subtask behaviors are readily available as building blocks. However, the available evaluation budget must be distributed across all subtasks, whereas a single generalist behavior can exploit the entire budget for its own optimization. items.title: Evolutionary Algorithm For Reservoir Learning And Yielding
items.summary: Reservoir computing, a type of recurrent neural network, is a promising approach for temporal learning as it separates dynamic processing from the trained readout layer. This paper introduces EARLY (Evolutionary Algorithm for Reservoir Learning and Yielding), a framework designed to evolve both the topology and hyperparameters of multi-reservoir ESNs. items.title: A Hybrid Classical-Quantum Annealing Algorithm for the TSP
items.summary: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms can help mitigating the physical limitations of current quantum devices, particularly the low qubit count and the reduced topological connectivity. In this paper, we propose a hybrid technique to solve a well-known NP-hard optimization problem: the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP). Our approach is based on a graph contraction technique that removes most of the dimensionality of the original problem instance, producing a sub-TSP of a size suitable to be efficiently solved by a quantum device. items.title: Diversifying Toxicity Search in Large Language Models Through Speciation
items.summary: Evolutionary prompt search is a practical black-box approach for red teaming large language models, however existing methods often collapse onto a small family of high-performing prompts, limiting coverage of distinct failure modes. We present a speciated quality-diversity extension of ToxSearch that maintains multiple high-toxicity prompt niches in parallel rather than optimizing a single best prompt. items.title: Discrete Gene Crossover Accelerates Solution Discovery in Quality-Diversity Algorithms
items.summary: Quality-Diversity (QD) algorithms aim to discover diverse, high-performing solutions across behavioral niches. However, QD search often stagnates as incremental variation operators struggle to propagate building blocks across large populations. Existing mutation operators rely on gradual variation to solutions, limiting their ability to efficiently explore regions of the search space distant from parent solutions or to spread beneficial genetic material through the population.
